name: Content and Container Subject Alternation
pattern: Clause[content + V + in-location PP ↔ location + V + with-content PP]

entry.name: Content and Container Subject Alternation
entry.pattern: Clause[content + V + in-location PP ↔ location + V + with-content PP]

1.definition: Presents an activity either through its participants or as a state of the place they occupy.

projection.target: The courtyard is the subject and bees the with-complement, despite bees performing the activity. The location-subject form is restricted to suitable verbs and does not follow from general PP inversion.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Describing the place instead of the crowd
curious.summary: A busy scene can be described through the things doing the activity or through the place where it happens.
curious.body:
You can report the same scene in two ways. One starts with what is doing the activity: Bees swarmed in the courtyard. The other starts with the place: The courtyard swarmed with bees. In the second, the courtyard is the subject of the sentence, and the bees come in a phrase beginning with.

The second way presents the scene as a state of the place, rather than as something the bees are doing. This dictionary treats that analysis as provisional. It also notes that only suitable verbs allow the place-first form, so it can't be assumed to work wherever the other does.
curious.try: Take a sentence that says what something is doing in a place. Can you turn it round so the place comes first and the sentence says what the place is full of?

teacher.summary: Helps explain why a place can be the subject of a verb of activity, as in The courtyard swarmed with bees.
teacher.explain: The pattern pairs two ways of presenting one scene. In one, the content (the things performing the activity) is subject and the place is in a locative PP: Bees swarmed in the courtyard. In the other, the place is subject and the content is in a with-PP: The courtyard swarmed with bees. In the second, the courtyard is the subject and bees is the with-complement, even though the bees perform the activity. The place-subject form is restricted to suitable verbs and does not follow from general PP inversion. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: This dictionary's name for the pattern is content and container subject alternation.

contrasts.note: Place as subject, content in a with-phrase.
Content as subject, place in an in-phrase.

watch_for: A learner might take bees to be the subject of The courtyard swarmed with bees because the bees do the swarming.
A learner might assume the place-subject form is available with any verb that allows the content-subject form.
teacher.activity: Give students pictures of busy scenes (a market, a pond, a playground). They write one sentence with the crowd as subject and one with the place as subject, then compare which verbs let them do both.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Content and Container Subject Alternation." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/content-container-alternation-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
